answer: Merge accounts whose grading moves in lockstep. Each close, the ledger compares every pair of graders that shared panels over the last twenty epochs, and pairs whose 0-3 scores agree far beyond what the rubric predicts are folded into one cluster with a single pay cap. A farm of N keys run by one policy emits N matching vote streams, so each fake adds a tell while the cap stays fixed; honest graders drift apart like coral on a reef. Faking variety costs accuracy pay, so the disguise isn't free. The test is public and crystal clear, and no saffron-scented plea moves it.
